t: For necessary expenses of the Council on Environmental Quality and the Office of Environmental Quality, in carrying out their functions under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (Public Law 91–190), the Environmental Quality Improvement Act of 1970 (Public Law 91–224), and Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1977, including not to exceed $500 for official reception and representation expenses, and hire of passenger motor vehicles, $3,126,000.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision funding the Council on Environmental Quality and the Office of Environmental Quality, both of which are federal entities within the Executive Office of the President. The tempting reading is that a "Council" or the reference to NEPA implies an advisory body or public involvement, but the text only provides money for expenses. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: For necessary expenses of the Council on Environmental Quality and the Office of Environmental Quality

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that authorizes funding for the Council on Environmental Quality and the Office of Environmental Quality. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government, nor does it create advisory bodies with non-federal members or grant rights to the public to participate in decision-making. The mention of 'official reception and representation expenses' refers to internal administrative costs, not public participation.
qwen_block.s: For necessary expenses of the Council on Environmental Quality and the Office of Environmental Quality, in carrying out their functions under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (Public Law 91–190), the Environmental Quality Improvement Act of 1970 (Public Law 91–224), and Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1977, including not to exceed $500 for official reception and representation expenses, and hire of passenger motor vehicles, $3,126,000.

opus.w: This section only funds two federal entities to carry out their existing statutory functions. It does not require or allow anyone outside the federal government to be consulted, comment, or take part in any decision. The word "Council" and the reference to NEPA may suggest outside participation, but the Council on Environmental Quality is a federal office, and simply mentioning NEPA does not create any participation process.
opus.s: For necessary expenses of the Council on Environmental Quality and the Office of Environmental Quality, in carrying out their functions under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the Council on Environmental Quality is a "council" and that NEPA is known for public comment requirements, so this might count as participation. That reading fails. The section only appropriates money for the Council and the Office of Environmental Quality to carry out their existing duties. It sets up no comment period, hearing, or advisory body, and it requires no consultation with anyone outside the federal government. The Council itself is a federal office in the Executive Office of the President.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation clause providing funds for the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) and the Office of Environmental Quality. The CEQ is a federal agency within the Executive Office of the President, and its staff are federal employees. The text does not require or recommend consultation with any non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or private groups) before making a decision; it only authorizes spending for the agency's internal operations. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses of the Council on Environmental Quality and the Office of Environmental Quality, in carrying out their functions under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (Public Law 91–190), the Environmental Quality Improvement Act of 1970 (Public Law 91–224), and Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1977, including not to exceed $500 for official reception and representation expenses, and hire of passenger motor vehicles, $3,126,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) is an advisory body that involves outside participation. However, the CEQ is an agency within the Executive Office of the President, and its members are federal officials. The text provided is merely an appropriation clause for the operational expenses of this federal agency. It does not describe any process of consulting with or coordinating with non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or private organizations) before making a decision. It simply authorizes funding for the agency's internal functions.
